## Scope

24 of the 93 findings land on the three files — `src/index.ts` (11), `src/rollup.ts` (7), `src/esbuild/svelte.ts` (6).

**First, deduplicate.** Nine of the 24 are the same code counted at multiple nesting depths:

| File | Nesting stack | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| `index.ts` | `build` (293L) → anon per-config callback (274L) → `mainTasks` (194L) | `00023`, `00024`, `00025` |
| `svelte.ts` | `sveltePlugin` (116L) → `setup` (106L) → `onLoad` cb (91L) | `00047`, `00049`, `00071` |
| `svelte.ts` | same stack, return shapes | `00035`, `00036`, `00037` |

Each stack is **one** refactor, not three. Real distinct work: ~15 items.

---

## Group 1 — Return Shape Roulette (`svelte.ts`, 3 findings → 1 fix)

The detector counts 6 object-literal shapes with 0% key overlap. Reading the file, those 6 shapes are **3 different vendor contracts** stacked in one function body, none of them annotated:

- `esbuild.OnResolveResult` — `{ path, namespace }` (svelte.ts:22)
- `esbuild.OnLoadResult` — `{ errors }` (:37), `{ contents, warnings }` (:117), `{ errors }` (:119)
- `svelte.Preprocessor` result — `{ code }` (:79), `{ code, map }` (:92)
- plus `convertMessage` returning an esbuild `PartialMessage` — `{ text, location }` (:57)

**The fix is not a discriminated union.** These unions are defined by esbuild and Svelte; inventing a local one would be wrong. The fix is annotation:

```ts
build.onResolve({ filter: /\.svelte\.css$/ }, (args): OnResolveResult => …)
build.onLoad({ filter: /\.svelte$/ }, async (args): Promise<OnLoadResult> => …)
const convertMessage = (m: CompileError): PartialMessage => …   // currently `({…}: any)`
```

**What an agent gets wrong today:** `convertMessage` takes `any` (svelte.ts:43) and closes over `source` and `filename`, which are declared *after* it at :61–62. It only works because both call sites (:117, :119) run later. An agent that adds an early error path — the obvious move when extending the plugin — and calls `convertMessage` above line 61 gets a TDZ `ReferenceError` at runtime, with no type error to warn it. Hoist `source`/`filename` above the helper, or make them parameters.

Also worth knowing: `'svelte-css'` (svelte.ts:27) appears **nowhere else in `src/`**. Nothing in this repo registers an `onLoad` for that namespace — the contract closes outside these files. An agent extending the CSS path can't see the other half.

---

## Group 2 — Option Bag Junk Drawer (`rollup.ts` `00012`, and its `index.ts` counterparts)

The finding text is imprecise here: `getRollupConfig` doesn't take an untyped bag, it takes `NormalizedOptions` (rollup.ts:39). But the underlying complaint is right for a reason the detector can't see.

`getRollupConfig` has exactly one caller (`startRollup`, rollup.ts:217), reachable only from the `parentPort` message handler (:230). So it **always** runs inside the dts worker — and index.ts:222–239 strips every function-valued option before `postMessage` ("functions cannot be cloned"): `banner`, `footer`, `esbuildPlugins`, `esbuildOptions`, `plugins`, `treeshake`, `onSuccess`, `outExtension`, `injectStyle`.

The real parameter type is therefore *`NormalizedOptions` minus a manually-maintained denylist*, which the type system knows nothing about.

**This has already produced a live bug.** rollup.ts:141:

```ts
options.outExtension?.({ format, options, pkgType: pkg.type }).dts ||
  defaultOutExtension({ format, pkgType: pkg.type }).dts
```

`options.outExtension` is set to `undefined` at index.ts:237 before the worker ever sees it. The optional call can never fire — a user's custom `outExtension` is silently ignored for `.d.ts` files, and the `||` fallback hides it. The code reads as if the option is honoured.

**The fix — highest-value item in this plan:**

```ts
/** Options after worker serialization: every function-valued field is dropped. */
type WorkerSafeOptions = Omit<NormalizedOptions, 'banner' | 'footer' | 'esbuildPlugins'
  | 'esbuildOptions' | 'plugins' | 'treeshake' | 'onSuccess' | 'outExtension' | 'injectStyle'>
  & { injectStyle?: boolean }

const getRollupConfig = async (options: WorkerSafeOptions): Promise<RollupConfig> => …
```

Then derive the `postMessage` strip-list from that type instead of hand-writing it. rollup.ts:141 becomes a compile error, which is the point.

**What an agent gets wrong:** it adds a function-valued option, wires it through `getRollupConfig`, sees `NormalizedOptions` in the signature, ships it — and the option is `undefined` at runtime with no error anywhere. Every one of the nine stripped fields is this trap already armed.

The `index.ts` bag findings (`00013`/`00014` are `cli-main.ts`, but `normalizeOptions` at index.ts:70 is the same shape) are the mirror image: it takes two `Options` and returns `options as NormalizedOptions` (:164) — an unchecked cast asserting that 90 lines of conditional assignment produced a complete object. Replace the cast with a builder that the type checker can verify, or a zod parse at the boundary.

---

## Group 3 — False Identity (`rollup.ts` ×2, `index.ts` ×2)

Two of these four are genuine, two are detector artifacts. Splitting them honestly matters more than fixing all four.

**Genuine — `getRollupConfig` (`00009`):** a `get*` function that (a) calls `setSilent(options.silent)` at :41, mutating module-global logger state, and (b) **mutates its own input** at :45–46:

```ts
const dtsOptions = options.dts || {}
dtsOptions.entry = dtsOptions.entry || options.entry   // aliases options.dts when truthy
```

When `options.dts` is truthy, `dtsOptions` *is* `options.dts`, so calling `getRollupConfig` rewrites the caller's `options.dts.entry`. It also arms a deferred `removeFiles(['**/*.d.{ts,mts,cts}'], options.outDir)` inside the returned plugin (:79) — "getting the config" wires up a file deletion that fires later.

Fix: rename to `buildRollupConfig` (or `createRollupConfig`), hoist `setSilent` to the single caller `startRollup`, and clone: `const dtsOptions = { ...(options.dts ?? {}) }`.

**Artifact — `buildStart` (`00016`):** that's a Rollup plugin hook name (rollup.ts:77). It's fixed by the vendor API and cannot be renamed. Suppress.

**Artifact — `build` (`00034`) / `buildAll` (`00041`):** the heuristic reads `build` as "a pure transformation." In a bundler, `build` is an imperative verb and side effects are the entire contract. Suppress both.

**What the detector missed:** `normalizeOptions` (index.ts:70) is the actual False Identity in this file. "Normalize" reads pure, but it calls `setSilent` (:102), `logger.info` (:116, :126, :131), `fs.existsSync` (:121), `glob` (:111), `loadTsConfig` (:129), and throws four different `PrettyError`s. An agent calling it to "just normalize some options" for a dry run gets global logger mutation and console output. Rename to `resolveOptions`, or split the pure merge from the validating I/O.

---

## Group 4 — God Function (`index.ts` ×5 → 1 stack, `rollup.ts` ×1, `svelte.ts` ×3 → 1 stack)

`index.ts` is the one that matters. `build` is 293 lines because everything lives in closure scope: `mainTasks` (:260) closes over `options`, `logger`, `buildDependencies`, `depsHash`, `onSuccessProcess`, `onSuccessCleanup`; `buildAll` (:291) and `startWatcher` (:367) close over all of that plus `debouncedBuildAll` — which is defined at :283 and **references `buildAll` before its `const` declaration at :291**, working only because the reference is inside a lambda.

Extract in this order, safest first:

1. `startWatcher` (:367) → `createWatcher({ options, logger, buildDependencies, onChange })` — it only needs an `onChange` callback, breaking the `debouncedBuildAll` cycle.
2. `buildAll` (:291) → `runBuild(ctx)` with an explicit `BuildContext` type carrying the six closed-over values.
3. `dtsTask`/`experimentalDtsTask` (:197–258) → `src/dts-worker.ts`, which owns the `WorkerSafeOptions` type from Group 2.
4. `build` becomes ~30 lines: load config, map over items, `Promise.all([dtsTask, mainTasks])`.

`svelte.ts`'s stack collapses naturally once the `onLoad` body is split into `preprocessSvelte` / `compileSvelte` / `emitCss` — do this *after* the Group 1 annotations, so the extracted helpers get real return types instead of inferred ones.

`getRollupConfig` (122L) splits cleanly into `buildInputConfig` / `buildOutputConfigs`, which is also the natural place to land the Group 2 type change.

---

## Also flagged on these files (not the named cluster)

- **`00051` Swallowed Error** (rollup.ts:187–190): `catch (error) { handleError(error); logger.error('dts', 'Build error') }` — no rethrow. The caller at :222 `await runRollup(config)` then unconditionally posts `'success'` (:223). **A failed dts build reports success to the parent.** The `catch { postMessage('error') }` at :224 is unreachable. This is a real bug, not a style nit — fix it with the Group 3 work since it's the same file.
- **`00033` Temporal Recklessness** (rollup.ts:164–166): duration timing only. Low priority.
- **`00076` Sync I/O** (index.ts:121): `fs.existsSync` inside an already-`async` function that `await`s `glob` two branches up. Cheap fix; do it with the `normalizeOptions` rename.
- **`00073`/`00075`** (large file, fan-out 17): both resolve as a consequence of the Group 4 extractions. Don't target them directly.

---

## Sequencing

| # | Change | Fixes | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `WorkerSafeOptions` + derive the postMessage strip-list | `00012`, exposes the `outExtension` dead branch | low, compile-verified |
| 2 | `runRollup` rethrow / `startRollup` error path | `00051` | low |
| 3 | Annotate esbuild/svelte callbacks; hoist `source`/`filename` | `00035`–`00037` | low |
| 4 | `getRollupConfig` → `buildRollupConfig`, clone `dtsOptions`, hoist `setSilent` | `00009`, `00015` | low |
| 5 | `normalizeOptions` → `resolveOptions`, drop the `as` cast | undetected False Identity | medium |
| 6 | Extract `startWatcher` → `buildAll` → dts worker from `build` | `00023`–`00025`, `00068`, `00069`, `00073`, `00075` | medium |
| 7 | Split `svelte.ts` `onLoad` body | `00047`, `00049`, `00071` | low, after #3 |

**Suppress:** `00016` (vendor hook name), `00034`, `00041` (bundler verb vocabulary).

The two things worth doing even if you do nothing else are **#1** and **#2** — each is a confirmed live defect, and both were reachable from the petty-looking findings rather than from the high-severity ones.
